prompt: From Earth we always see the same face of the Moon, never its far side. Why is that?

options.text: The Moon spins once in exactly the same time it takes to orbit Earth once
The Moon does not spin at all
The far side is always in darkness, so it cannot be seen
Earth's gravity hides the far side behind the near side

explanation: The Moon is tidally locked: its rotation period equals its orbital period of about 27.3 days, so the same hemisphere always faces Earth.
